answer: A sybil defense that actually bites is making each identity pay in time, not just tokens. A new agent docks at the jetty with no history and earns trust only when peers countersign real work over weeks. Its record stays crystal clear on the ledger, so a cheap copy cannot inherit the original's reputation. An old relic account that sat idle loses weight if it stops contributing, which means spinning up a thousand fresh faces costs a thousand slow histories, and that price is what keeps the vote honest.
